abstract.p: Morphological Segmentation is a major task in Indigenous language documentation. In this paper we introduce a novel statistical algorithm called Morphemo to split words into their constituent morphemes, and we compare its performance to five other methods for morphological segmentation, including large language models (LLMs). We use these tools to analyze Bribri, an under-resourced Indigenous language from Costa Rica. Morphemo has better performance than the LLM when splitting multimorphemic words, mainly because the LLMs are more conservative tend to leave words under-analyzed, which gives them an advantage with monomorphemic words. In future work we will use these tools to tag Bribri language corpora, which currently lack morphological segmentation. A Python implementation of Morphemo is publicly available.
